source_meta._title: Cauldrons filled with water, lava or powder snow cannot be used as a workstation for villagers

stor.recommended_version: Minecraft Java Edition snapshot 21w11a. Use this as the primary reproduction version because it is the latest version listed in the report's affected-version range. Do not substitute 21w13a or a later version.
stor.environment: Single-player Java Edition world in Creative mode with cheats enabled, preferably a newly generated Superflat world with structures disabled. Run the reproduction independently three times: once with a Water Bucket, once with a Lava Bucket, and once with a Powder Snow Bucket. Use a fresh world for each variant to prevent prior villager job-site state from affecting the next run.
preconditions: Install and launch the exact Java Edition snapshot 21w11a from the Minecraft Launcher.
Use an unmodified client without mods or non-default datapacks that change villagers, professions, cauldrons, schedules, or block interactions.
Create a separate fresh world for each filling-material variant: water, lava, and powder snow.
Set Game Mode to Creative and enable cheats so the required blocks, items, spawn egg, and time commands are available.
Prefer the Superflat world type and disable structure generation so no village or unrelated workstation blocks are near the test location.
The test villager must be an adult unemployed villager, not a baby, nitwit, or already employed villager.
Do not place any other villager workstation blocks in the test world.
Do not trade with the villager. Trading can lock its profession and alter the job-site test condition.
Perform the trigger only after the villager has visibly become a leatherworker and the leatherworker trade interface has been used to confirm the profession.

steps.action: In the Minecraft Launcher, select the installation for Java Edition snapshot 21w11a and start the game. Confirm the version displayed on the title screen before continuing.
steps.success_cue: The Minecraft title screen identifies the running version as 21w11a.

steps.action: Select Singleplayer, choose Create New World, and configure a fresh Creative-mode test world. Enable cheats. For a controlled environment, select the Superflat world type and turn Generate Structures off. Create the world.
steps.exact_input: Game Mode: Creative; Allow Cheats: ON; World Type: Superflat; Generate Structures: OFF
steps.success_cue: The player has spawned in a new, flat world and can fly and instantly break blocks.

steps.action: Wait before setting up the test until the nearby terrain has rendered and movement responds normally.
steps.success_cue: The ground around the player is visible, no chunk-loading screen is present, and normal movement and inventory controls respond immediately.

steps.action: Set the world to daytime so the villager can enter its normal job-site acquisition period. Press T to open chat, type the command exactly with the leading slash, and press Enter.
steps.success_cue: The world changes to daytime and the command reports successful time adjustment.

steps.action: Keep the test at daytime. Press T, enter the gamerule command exactly with the leading slash, and press Enter.
steps.success_cue: Chat confirms that the doDaylightCycle gamerule is now false and the sun no longer advances.

steps.action: Open the Creative inventory with E. Obtain one Cauldron and place it in an accessible hotbar slot. The hotbar is the row of nine item slots along the bottom of the screen.
steps.success_cue: A Cauldron item is visible in one of the nine hotbar slots.

steps.action: While the Creative inventory is open, obtain one Villager Spawn Egg and place it in another hotbar slot.
steps.success_cue: A Villager Spawn Egg is visible in the hotbar.

steps.action: Obtain the bucket required for the current independent variant and place it in the hotbar. Use a Water Bucket for the first run, a Lava Bucket in a fresh second run, and a Powder Snow Bucket in a fresh third run.
steps.exact_input: Run 1: Water Bucket; Run 2: Lava Bucket; Run 3: Powder Snow Bucket
steps.success_cue: Exactly one of the specified filled buckets for the current run is available in the hotbar.

steps.action: Close the inventory with E. Move to an open, level location where no other workstation blocks or villagers are visible nearby.
steps.success_cue: The player is standing in a clear test area with no village structures, villagers, or other workstation blocks nearby.

steps.action: Select the Cauldron in the hotbar, aim at the top surface of a ground block, and use the place-block control, which is right-click by default, once.
steps.success_cue: One empty cauldron is standing upright on the ground with open space beside it.

steps.action: Select the Villager Spawn Egg in the hotbar. Aim at the ground directly beside the empty cauldron and right-click once to spawn a villager.
steps.exact_input: Right-click once while holding Villager Spawn Egg
steps.success_cue: One villager is present beside the empty cauldron.

steps.action: Inspect the spawned villager before proceeding. It must be an adult unemployed villager. If it is a baby, wears the green nitwit robe, or already displays an unrelated profession outfit, remove it without changing the cauldron and spawn a replacement beside the cauldron. Repeat until a suitable adult unemployed villager is present.
steps.success_cue: A single adult villager that is neither a nitwit nor visibly assigned to another profession is beside the empty cauldron.

steps.action: Do not fill the cauldron yet. Wait while the villager can reach or stand near the empty cauldron. Continue only after it adopts the leatherworker profession; profession acquisition may be accompanied by green particles and a change to the leatherworker outfit.
steps.success_cue: The villager has changed from unemployed to the leatherworker profession while the cauldron is still empty.

steps.action: Confirm the profession without completing a trade. With an empty hand or any non-interacting item selected, aim at the villager and right-click once to open its trading interface. Verify that the interface identifies it as a novice leatherworker, then close the interface with Esc. Do not place an item into a trade slot and do not take any trade output.
steps.exact_input: Right-click villager; verify Leatherworker/Novice; press Esc
steps.success_cue: The trade interface has confirmed that the villager is a leatherworker, no trade has been completed, and the normal world view is open again.

steps.action: Select the filled bucket assigned to the current run in the hotbar. Verify visually that the cauldron is still empty before using the bucket.
steps.exact_input: Water Bucket, Lava Bucket, or Powder Snow Bucket for the current run
steps.success_cue: The chosen filled bucket is held in the player's active hand, the confirmed leatherworker remains near the test site, and the cauldron is still empty.

steps.action: Aim directly at the inside or upper rim of the empty cauldron and use the bucket once with the use-item control, which is right-click by default. Do not interact with the villager or cauldron again after this click.
steps.exact_input: Right-click the empty cauldron once with the selected Water Bucket, Lava Bucket, or Powder Snow Bucket
steps.success_cue: The same cauldron that served as the confirmed leatherworker workstation now visibly contains the selected water, lava, or powder snow material.

stor.handoff_condition: The selected bucket has just been used once on the previously empty cauldron after that cauldron was confirmed as the villager's leatherworker job site. The cauldron visibly contains the selected material. Stop all player input and begin observation immediately. Repeat the complete plan in separate fresh worlds for the other two bucket variants.
uncertainties: The report does not specify a world seed, world type, game mode, enclosure, or exact time of day. A fresh Creative Superflat world with structures disabled and frozen daytime is a practical deterministic setup rather than a stated report requirement.

The original reproduction bullets explicitly say to add water or lava. Powder snow is added by the issue title, affected-version information, and the later report comment stating that powder snow cauldrons are additionally affected.

The report does not state a fixed delay for villager profession acquisition. The plan therefore uses the visible leatherworker profession and its trade-interface label as the readiness condition instead of relying on an arbitrary waiting period.

The three filling materials are treated as independent variants. A fresh world per material is recommended to avoid profession locking, stale job-site memory, or block state left by a previous variant.
